messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: Triggered page for HIGH: inference-queue.backlog > 5000 across inference-prod-pool (policy: queue-depth-threshold). Links: https://pagerduty.local/incidents/PD12345 and runbook: <https://runbook.internal/autoscaler-queue#triage>
maya: acked on-call. seeing 10k+ pending requests on the dashboard. latency SLOs breached for several customers.
jordan: looking at autoscaler logs now. initial hypothesis: node provision lag + provider quota throttle. running `redwoodctl autoscaler status --pool inference-prod`
maya: paste of `redwoodctl autoscaler status` output: `state=active queued=10234 desired=120 nodes=8 provisioning=0`
sam: provisioning=0 looks wrong. kube events show node requests stuck Pending in cloud provider. suspect hitting per-account node quota.
lee: @sam can you check cloud console quota and pending node count? I can attempt temporary fallback to smaller model to shed GPU memory per work unit.
sam: checked quota: current quota 12, used 12. autoscaler requested 4 but provider rejected. raising request with cloud support would take too long.
jordan: mitigation plan: 1) manual provision of 2 preemptible nodes (if allowed) 2) enable burst-capacity override for 10m 3) route non-critical tenants to fallback v1-small model.
maya: I'll trigger burst override now: `redwoodctl capacity burst --pool inference-prod --nodes 4 --duration 10m --reason "pagerduty queue surge"`
incident-bot: Action logged: burst override requested by maya. awaiting provider acceptance.
lee: while we wait, I pushed a temporary routing rule: `route:tenant_tags -> model=v1-small` for non-SLA tenants. That should reduce average tokens.
jordan: monitoring: pending backlog dropped from 10.2k -> 6.1k in 6m after routing change. latency still high for priority tenants.
sam: provider accepted 2 preemptible nodes. `kubectl get nodes` shows +2 nodes ready. autoscaler desired now met partially.
maya: good. I'm going to start draining oldest queued jobs for low-priority customers to free KV cache pressure: `redwoodctl jobs cancel --age > 5m --tag low-priority`
lee: FYI added a note to runbook that quota exhaustion happened due to spike from internal load test that should have been gated. Runbook PR: <https://git.internal/runbooks/changes/234>
sre-lead: escalating to secondary on-call for follow-through and postmortem. @jordan please hand off next steps: confirm burst rollback time, verify fallback routing cleanup, and prepare short customer impact blurb.
jordan: handoff ack. next steps I will: 1) confirm burst rollback at +10m 2) remove routing rule once backlog < 500 and priority latency stable 3) collect traces for affected tenants 4) draft customer note.
maya: paging summary for handoff: incident triggered by queue-depth-threshold -> quota prevented autoscaler from scaling -> manual burst + preemptible nodes + routing to v1-small reduced backlog -> partial customer impact: elevated latency for premium tenants ~7-12m window, some 5xx from low-priority jobs.
sre-lead: tagging this for follow-up postmortem, add runbook gap: auto-detect provider quota and preempt automatic fallback to burst.
jordan: customer note draft: "We experienced elevated request latency and intermittent errors for a subset of inference requests between 12:33 and 12:45 UTC caused by capacity provisioning delays. We mitigated with temporary burst capacity and routing fallbacks; normal service restored by 12:46 UTC."
incident-bot: PagerDuty: incident PD12345 acknowledged by maya and escalated to jordan.
maya: handing off to jordan for next 30m. I'm going offline for on-call rotation. :wave:
jordan: taking over. I will update last_message_ts when incident closed.
(autoscaler metrics snippet): `queue_depth: 10234 -> 420 -> 180 over 15m, desired_nodes: 120 -> 128 (requested) -> 126 (provisioned)`
jordan: closing actions noted in ticket: file postmortem, add quota alert, add test-gate for internal load tests.
incident-bot: Incident closed by jordan. Duration 0h0m53s from first ack to mitigations in place.
